plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates first-order gain magnitude and lag from a mid-level hold, which is required to choose any steady-state feedforward and feedback timing for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with self-cooling hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.21 toward ~0.4-0.55 with visible lag, slope decreasing over the hold; end slope indicates whether equilibrium is reached.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures zero-input decay, ambient level, and cooling time constant, which determines integral and hold requirements for control and cannot be inferred from heating alone.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-cooling hypothesis is right, y will fall exponentially from ~0.51 toward ~0.2 with time constant tens of seconds, reaching ~0.24-0.32 after 180s with slope flattening toward zero; if no self-decay, y will stay near 0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests linearity and steady-state gain at a second amplitude distinct from 0.5, needed to interpolate feedforward to hold target 0.5 and to rule out dead-zone at low-mid inputs.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain linear hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.32 toward ~0.36-0.42 with ~15-20s lag then slowing rise; end slope near zero indicates approach to equilibrium for u=0.3. Flat response would indicate dead-zone, rise toward >0.45 would indicate non-linear high gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Resolves steady-state gain at u=0.3 and settling time/linearity vs u=0.5, which determines feedforward to hold 0.5 and feedback timing; continued hold isolates equilibrium from transient without a new step.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.40 toward ~0.42-0.47 with slope decaying toward ~0 over the hold; continued steep rise would indicate higher gain/longer tau, flat would indicate early equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Resolves steady-state feedforward needed to hold target 0.5 by testing an intermediate level between 0.3 and 0.5 starting from band edge, which determines controller bias and cannot be interpolated reliably until measured.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain ~0.7-0.9 and tau ~100-170s hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.47 toward ~0.50-0.53 with decaying slope over the hold, ending in or very near band 0.475-0.525; flat at ~0.47 would indicate saturation, fast rise above 0.55 would indicate higher gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Pins steady-state feedforward needed to hold target 0.5 by testing u=0.34 from band edge, discriminating between 0.3 holding ~0.469 and 0.5 overshooting, which is required for controller bias and cannot be interpolated reliably until measured.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain ~0.9, tau ~160-180s hypothesis is right, y will rise slowly from ~0.47 toward ~0.50-0.52 with decaying slope over the 180s hold, ending in band 0.475-0.525 with small positive slope; flat at ~0.47 would imply saturation, fast rise above 0.55 would imply higher gain.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases y (positive static gain): higher heater power produces higher steady-state temperature.
Step response has observable lag with dead-time ~15-40s and dominant time constant ~130-180s, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: even moderate u around 0.3-0.5 produces a measurable rise above ambient.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.2 or below due to heat loss to the room.
Response is approximately linear across input levels for control purposes: average gain ~0.9 from ambient and incremental gain ~1.4 between u=0.3 and 0.34, consistent within 20-30%.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.32: u=0.3 settles at 0.469 with zero slope and u=0.34 settles at 0.526 with ~0 slope, bracketing the band.
Sensor noise on y is small (~0.005-0.01) so trends and end-slope in measured_summary are interpretable.
